Subject: Helios RFI: sampling & redaction questions

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the questionnaire. Our assurance lead reviewed the SOC 2 / SIG sections and asked a couple of clarifying questions before we accept the artifact package:

1) Can you confirm your proposed evidence sampling approach for operational controls (we typically ask for a 5–10% sample across last 6 months)?
2) We need a written redaction policy and a short explanation of who performs redaction and what pieces are considered sensitive by default.
3) Please include the acceptance criteria we should use when validating an evidence item (e.g., log retention retention window, timestamp format, proof of access control).

We have a tight window; can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff with your team tomorrow morning (Nov 2) to lock the plan?

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heliosfinancial.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Helios RFI: sampling & redaction questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and in the attached playbook:

- Sampling: we propose a risk-weighted sampling approach — baseline 5% of transactions/logs across the last 6 months, increasing to 10% for high-risk controls (privileged access, key rotation, KMS events).
- Redaction: redaction is performed by our Compliance Operations team using a documented checklist; default sensitive fields include PII (SSN, DOB), customer content, and private keys.
- Acceptance criteria: evidence must include an auditable timestamp, a clear owner, and an immutable reference (log id, snapshot id).

I attached an evidence_sampling_plan.xlsx and a short redaction_guidelines.docx that spell the approach and acceptance checks out. Happy to walk through tomorrow at 9:30am PT if that works for your team.

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0133
